title: Fix Puzzle 2D Performance Regression (Round 3 — Dirty-Scope + Batched refresh-ui)
description: Puzzle 2D board used to be very performant at the `premigration` git tag; after the migration from the bespoke `puzzle/2d/react/index.tsx` renderer to the generic framework shell + Rust/WASM BoardHost pipeline, zoom and selection now take multiple seconds. Root-cause refactor per plan at /Users/ueli/.claude/plans/puzzle-2d-used-to-piped-balloon.md: (1) restore rAF-coalesced rendering in framework/renderer/react/components/puzzle-2d-board-host.tsx (no more synchronous renderFrame()/dispatch per raw pointer/wheel event), (2) stop hover setters from bumping content_scene_generation in mathematical/graph/port/directed/normal/rs/lib.rs, (3) stop puzzle/plugin/rs/lib.rs from re-stringifying the whole fixture 3x per action, (4) parallelize framework/renderer/react/os-shell.tsx refreshUi()'s sequential awaits, (5) add spatial partitioning to hit-testing in the graph engine.
summary:
Implemented the deferred Round 2 follow-ups: a generic dirty-scope protocol and a batched, hash-conditional refresh-ui WIT call, replacing the shell's ~12 sequential per-action WASM round trips (render ×6 bodies + tools ×3 + windowEngagements + windowMeasures + appLabels) with one call per action.

**1. UiDirtyScope protocol** (framework/core/rs/lib.rs, framework/plugin/rs/lib.rs, framework/core/js/index.ts): a `Full | None | Partial{windowBodies, panelBodies, tools, engagements, measures, labels}` enum on `ActionResult`/`ActionEmit`/`ActionResponse`, defaulting to `Full` so every plugin that doesn't opt in keeps today's behavior untouched. puzzle2d's `handle_action` now declares narrow scopes per action (select → 3 panes + layers/properties panels + engagements; camera → 3 panes only; nodeMove/structural board events → panes + properties/layers + measures/engagements as appropriate; LOD/grid/brush settings → panes + measures; cold-tier actions like addNode/deleteSelection/setActiveExample stay Full). The s plugin's presenceHeartbeat scopes to None (it only records identity, never needs a re-render).

**2. Batched refresh-ui WIT call** (framework/wit/world.wit, framework/plugin/rs/lib.rs, framework/product/os/dev/script.ts, framework/core/js/index.ts): deleted the four now-dead per-section exports (list-tools, window-engagements, window-measures, app-labels) and their record types; added one `refresh-ui(instance-id, request) -> response` call. The request lists every window/panel/engagements/measures/labels section the host wants with the fnv1a-64 content hash it already holds; the response omits the payload for any section whose hash still matches, so an unchanged section costs one hash compare instead of a full re-render/re-serialize/re-parse. Regenerated the jco bridge and worker templates; `PluginWasmHandle.refreshUi` replaces the four deleted methods in the JS handle (both the component-model and worker-backed loader paths, plus `pluginHandleForBridge`).

**3. Scope-aware shell refreshUi** (framework/renderer/react/os-shell.tsx): `refreshUi`/`refreshSpawnedUi` now build one batched request via new exported pure helpers `buildUiRefreshRequest`/`applyUiRefreshResponseToCache`, backed by a per-session-instance `UiRefreshCache` (Map keyed by section:key → {hash, value}), cleared on session switch. `uiScope` threads from `ActionResponse` through `applyHostEffects` into both refresh paths. Unrequested/unchanged sections keep their exact prior object reference from cache, composing with Round 2's `mergeRecordPreservingIdentity`/`InterpretedUiNode` memo so React actually bails on them.

**Three real bugs found and fixed during live verification** (direct plugin-module testing in the browser against the actual compiled artifact, bypassing the app shell): (a) the `tools` field was designed but never actually added to the Rust `RefreshRequest`/`RefreshResponse` structs — caught via a live round-trip test; resolved by dropping tools handling entirely for now since `PluginApp`/`DocumentApp` currently expose no object-safe `tools()` accessor (mid-refactor by another session toward a declarative `mode_tools()` builder, unrelated to this ticket) and no puzzle2d scope ever requests it. (b) all puzzle2d scope helpers populated `window_bodies` with the pane/kind-id constants (`2d-overview` etc.) instead of the window body-key constants (`puzzle2d.play.overview` etc.) that the shell's `buildUiRefreshRequest` actually matches against — silently meant every partial scope would request zero window bodies; fixed by introducing `PUZZLE2D_WINDOW_BODY_KEYS` and using it consistently, with a regression test locking in the exact expected values. (c) `#[serde(rename_all = \"camelCase\")]` on the `UiDirtyScope` enum only renames variant names via `tag`, not fields inside a struct variant, so `Partial`'s fields silently serialized as snake_case (`window_bodies`) while the TS type expected camelCase (`windowBodies`) — a wire-format desync with no compile-time signal; fixed with `rename_all_fields = \"camelCase\"` (serde 1.0.228, well above the 1.0.128 minimum) and locked in with two new framework-core tests.

**Verified**: direct browser testing against the rebuilt puzzle-plugin WASM confirmed the full pipeline end-to-end — a select action's `handleAction` declares the correct `{kind:\"partial\", windowBodies:[...], panelBodies:[...], engagements:true}` scope with correct camelCase body-key values, and the resulting single batched `refreshUi` call correctly fetches only those sections; a repeat call with matching hashes shrank a 484,987-byte full response to 464 bytes (hash-only, no payload) confirming hash-conditional omission works. 40/40 puzzle-plugin Rust tests and 2/2 new framework-core UiDirtyScope tests passed in isolated runs; 119/120 framework-renderer-react tests pass (1 pre-existing, unrelated failure in `resolveWindowEngagement` from a stale test fixture, not touched by this work) including 6 new refresh-ui protocol tests and 7 carried-over Round 2 identity-preservation tests; lint clean.

**Blocked, not caused by this work**: repeated full-workspace and per-crate cargo runs during this session hit cascading compile failures in `cad-plugin`, `s-plugin`, `framework-renderer-wgpu`, and (in the final verification pass) the shared `ui_wgpu` crate itself — all from an actively in-progress concurrent refactor unrelated to this ticket (a `ToolCategory`/`PluginApp::tools()` → declarative `mode_tools()` migration, and separately a `loading: bool` field being added to several `ui_wgpu` UI node types mid-edit, confirmed via git log as commit \"270\" landing during this session). This blocked getting a single clean `cargo test --workspace`/`cargo build` run at any one moment near the end of the session, and blocked verifying the s-plugin presenceHeartbeat scope test via `cargo test` (though the change itself is a small, mechanically-correct addition following the exact pattern already proven working in puzzle-plugin). The puzzle-plugin and framework-core crates this ticket owns compiled and tested cleanly in isolated windows before this churn started, and the actual deliverable (the rebuilt puzzle_plugin_component wasm/js bundle) was verified working via live browser testing against the real compiled artifact.
